params.body:
`website/contact`, the "Stel een vraag" form of the website widget, is exempt from the request-forgery check because the iframe cannot rely on our session cookie. It had no other guard: any POST with a dealer hash, which is on every page that embeds the widget, opened a lead and mailed the garage, for any vehicle id, with no length limit and no throttle.

## What changes

- `App\Support\WidgetLeadGate`: the traps the StockCars site already uses on its own forms. A hidden honeypot (`bot-field`), an encrypted render moment in `form_token` that must be 4 seconds to 24 hours old (the modal is fetched on the click), at most 2 links in the message and none in the name.
- `WebsiteController::storeLead`: a refused post gets the same JSON as a sent one, so a bot learns nothing; the log keeps only the reason. The car must be the dealer's own or one its widget lists (`PublicWebsiteStock`), the same rule as the public API's lead endpoint; anything else is a 404.
- `LeadRequest`: the length limits of the public API (name 255, phone 60, email 255, message 5000).
- Route: `throttle:10,1`. The visitor's browser posts directly, so this counts per visitor.
- The `listings` read tool also returns `lead_sources`: leads per door (`public_api`, `widget`, `proposal`, `unknown`) against the period before, counts only. Spam through one door then shows on the B1 read without naming a garage or a person.

## Checked

- New tests: seven spam cases that answer 200 but open no lead and send no mail; another garage's car is a 404; leads are counted per source. The existing widget lead test now carries a token.
- Full suite on the workbench: 3040 tests, no failures or errors.

The site's own door (public API) is covered in stocklistdealer-eu/stockcars-website#38.

Closes #981
params.title: Guard the widget's question form against spam; count leads per source
